Mutation Enrichment Analysis: Responder vs Non-Responder (Anti-PD-1 Melanoma WES)
==================================================================================

COHORT: 38 patients (21 responders, 17 non-responders) with whole-exome sequencing
METHOD: Fisher's exact test (two-sided) per gene, 5,011 genes tested, BH-FDR correction

KEY FINDING: No genes reach FDR significance (q < 0.05) after multiple-testing correction,
due to the small cohort size (38 patients, 5,011 tests). However, the pre-computed
enrichment results (S1E) and nominal Fisher's exact tests identify the following patterns:

MUTATIONS ENRICHED IN RESPONDERS (pAdjR < 0.05 in S1E):
---------------------------------------------------------
13 genes show significant enrichment in responders after FDR correction in the original analysis.
The top 7 with the strongest evidence:

  FREM1   - 10/21 R (47.6%) vs 1/17 NR (5.9%), OR=14.55, pAdjR=1.09e-03
  OR13C5  -  7/21 R (33.3%) vs 0/17 NR (0%),    pAdjR=1.75e-04
  FMO1    -  7/21 R (33.3%) vs 0/17 NR (0%),    pAdjR=1.98e-03
  UTRN    -  7/21 R (33.3%) vs 0/17 NR (0%),    pAdjR=1.98e-03
  SP140L  -  6/21 R (28.6%) vs 0/17 NR (0%),    pAdjR=5.55e-03
  ITGA9   -  6/21 R (28.6%) vs 0/17 NR (0%),    pAdjR=5.55e-03
  SCN5A   -  9/21 R (42.9%) vs 1/17 NR (5.9%),  pAdjR=1.00e-01 (nominal p=0.012)

Additional FDR-significant in S1E: ZNF534, AMER3, LPHN3, ABCA7, OR10J1, BRCA2, MUC12

MUTATIONS ENRICHED IN NON-RESPONDERS (pAdjNR < 0.05 in S1E):
--------------------------------------------------------------
  CLEC14A - 0/21 R (0%)   vs 5/17 NR (29.4%), pAdjNR=0.029
  TRPM2   - 1/21 R (4.8%) vs 6/17 NR (35.3%), pAdjNR=0.047

Additional NR-enriched at nominal significance: ITGAX (0 vs 5, p=0.012),
PLEKHA7 (1 vs 5, p=0.003), DGKI (1 vs 5, p=0.005)

CANONICAL MELANOMA DRIVERS: No response association
-----------------------------------------------------
  BRAF  - 11 R / 9 NR (OR=0.98, p=1.00) — no enrichment
  NRAS  -  6 R / 3 NR (OR=1.87, p=0.48) — trend toward R, not significant
  NF1   -  6 R / 2 NR (OR=3.00, p=0.26) — trend toward R, not significant

BACKGROUND COMPARISON:
  FREM1 (R-enriched):  47.6% in R vs 12.4% Hodis, 9.2% CGAN
  OR13C5 (R-enriched): 33.3% in R vs 3.3% Hodis, 3.0% CGAN
  CLEC14A (NR-enriched): 29.4% in NR vs 4.1% Hodis, 4.5% CGAN

CAVEATS:
- Small cohort (38 patients) limits power; all nominal results are exploratory
- No FDR-significant hits from independent Fisher's exact re-analysis (q all = 1.0)
- Results are consistent with S1E but cannot be independently validated at this cohort size
- These are statistical associations, not proven causal drivers of response

The independent Fisher's exact re-analysis across 5,011 genes (38 patients, 21R/17NR) yielded no FDR-significant hits after multiple-testing correction, consistent with the small cohort size. Background mutation frequencies from independent melanoma cohorts (Hodis 2012, TCGA 2015) confirm that genes like FREM1 and OR13C5 are mutated at far higher rates in responders than expected.
